name: Melorheostosis

criteria.description: Characteristic flowing hyperostosis along the cortex of long bones on radiographs
Presence of localized bone pain and deformity in affected limbs
Histopathological evidence of sclerosing bone dysplasia with thickened cortical bone
Exclusion of other sclerosing bone dysplasias such as osteopathia striata or osteopoikilosis

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Radiographic flowing hyperostosis plus clinical symptoms of pain or deformity, with exclusion of other sclerosing bone dysplasias
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing may assist but no definitive mutation identified in all cases; diagnosis primarily clinical and radiographic

pathognomonic.symptomName: Localized bone pain in affected limb

common.symptomName: Joint stiffness adjacent to affected bone

occasional.symptomName: Skin changes overlying affected bone (hyperpigmentation or thickening)
Reduced range of motion in adjacent joints

rare.symptomName: Vascular malformations adjacent to affected bone

laboratory: Typically normal laboratory studies; no specific biomarkers
imaging: Radiographs showing characteristic flowing hyperostosis resembling 'dripping candle wax' along cortex of long bones
CT and MRI may show cortical thickening and soft tissue involvement
genetic: Somatic mutations in MAP2K1 gene identified in some cases, but not universally present
other: Histopathology reveals dense, sclerotic cortical bone with irregular remodeling

distinguishingFeatures: Linear striations in metaphyseal regions on radiographs
Multiple small, round or ovoid sclerotic foci scattered in epiphyses and metaphyses
No limb deformity or flowing hyperostosis

redFlags: Neurological deficits due to nerve compression
references: Leri A, Joanny J. Sur une affection non décrite des os: hyperostose en coulée des os longs. Bull Mem Soc Med Hop Paris. 1922;46:1141-1145.
Hellemans J, et al. Somatic mutations in MAP2K1 cause melorheostosis. Nat Commun. 2018;9(1):1390.
